newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RUGBY UNION-MANAGER DENIES LOMU WILL QUIT TOUR.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-MANAGER DENIES LOMU WILL QUIT TOUR.

text.p: Speculation that New Zealand rugby powerhouse Jonah Lomu will pull out of the Barbarians' tour of England this month was rubbished by his manager on Friday.
Press reports said the giant All Black winger was so upset by his one-week suspension for a dangerous tackle that he had threatened to boycott the tour.
Lomu's manager, Phil Kingsley-Jones, denied the report.

"That's rubbish," he told the New Zealand Press Association. "All we were afraid of was that he might be suspended for six weeks and he might not be able to go. There's never been any doubt about his availability."

Lomu was found guilty earlier this week by a rugby union judicial hearing of a "spear" tackle in a match last weekend. The suspension will prevent him from playing for his Counties-Manukau side in the final of the National Provincial Championship against Auckland on Sunday.
The one-week ban, which Lomu's provincial union believes is too harsh, has caused a national controversy and is under appeal.

New Zealand is sending a powerful All Black-packed Barbarians side on the two-match tour of England. The Barbarians will play the North of England on November 24 followed by a match against England at Twickenham six days later.
